exposure: Maternal infection with live porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (MIA)
outcome: Fetal microglial major histocompatibility complex class II expression
Sexual dimorphisms in microglial gene expression
cohort: Swine fetuses obtained from sows that underwent maternal immune activation (MIA) via viral infection.
finding: Maternal viral infection significantly alters fetal microglia, including reduced brain weights, altered microglial activity, and differential gene expression, suggesting a mechanism by which MIA impacts prenatal brain development and function, with sex-dependent consequences.
cross-section timing: 7 and 21 days post-maternal viral inoculation (during gestation)
